subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should OpenClaw permanently trust ClawHub, bundled metadata, and official-catalog mappings without this warning while requiring shell acknowledgement for every other first-install source and refusing those sources from chat and Crestodian?
rationale: The implementation and proof are strong, but the executable-code trust set and deliberate noninteractive compatibility break are product-security choices that cannot be inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Approve Proposed Boundary
options.body: Adopt the centralized classifier and documented acknowledgement workflow after refreshing review against current main.

options.title: Preserve Existing Defaults
options.body: Keep warnings but make fail-closed unattended and chat behavior opt-in to avoid an immediate compatibility break.

options.title: Narrow Frictionless Trust
options.body: Require acknowledgement for additional source classes until stronger publisher or integrity guarantees are defined.

recommendation.title: Approve Proposed Boundary
recommendation.body: Adopt the centralized classifier and documented acknowledgement workflow after refreshing review against current main.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history places the central plugin install, catalog, and chat-management implementation with this owner, giving the strongest evidence for the cross-surface policy decision.
